title: // C2 Frameworks Deep Dive

title: // Payload Development
description: The payload is what runs on the target. Loaders, shellcode, and delivery mechanisms determine whether you get caught in seconds or maintain access for months.

cards.title: Shellcode Generation
cards.summary: Raw position-independent code - the foundation of every payload

items.text: Attacks → Packages → Windows Executable (Stageless) → Raw
Convert .NET assemblies, PE files, VBS, JS into position-independent shellcode
Donut -i beacon.exe -o beacon.bin -a 2 -f 1 - x64, raw format
Shellcode Reflective DLL Injection - convert any DLL to shellcode
Write your own in C/Rust - avoid known signatures entirely

Use Windows callbacks to trigger shellcode (EnumFonts, CreateFiber, etc.)
C/C++ (smallest, fastest), Rust (safe + small), Nim (emerging), Go (cross-platform)

title: // Stealth & Impairment
description: Modern EDRs hook userland APIs, scan memory, inspect call stacks, and correlate telemetry. Every technique here addresses a specific detection mechanism.

callouts.title: EDR Detection Layers (6):
callouts.body: Static Signatures → Userland Hooks → ETW Telemetry → Kernel Callbacks → Memory Scanning → Behavioral/Call Stack. Effective evasion addresses all layers, not just AV signatures.

cards.title: AMSI Bypass
cards.summary: Antimalware Scan Interface - scans PowerShell, .NET, VBScript, JScript at runtime

items.text: Overwrite first bytes with `ret` - all scans return clean
Set BP on AmsiScanBuffer, modify args in exception handler - no memory patch needed
Internally modifies memory perms, avoids VirtualProtect trigger
Defender detects `C3` written to function prologues - use `POP RAX; JMP RAX`
Null-AMSI: Uses .NET Reflection to set `amsiInitFailed` - all subsequent scans return clean
AMSI patch must happen before loading any .NET tools or PS scripts

cards.title: Direct / Indirect Syscalls
cards.summary: Call the kernel directly - bypass all userland hooks entirely

items.text: Embed syscall instruction in your code - never touch ntdll.dll
Jump to the syscall instruction inside ntdll.dll - legitimate return address
SysWhispers3: Generate syscall stubs with multiple bypass options
HellsGate: Dynamically resolve syscall numbers at runtime from ntdll
HalosGate: Resolve syscall numbers even when ntdll is hooked (neighbor stub technique)
Direct syscalls have return address outside ntdll - detectable by stack analysis

cards.title: Sleep Obfuscation
cards.summary: Encrypt the implant in memory during sleep - evade periodic memory scans

items.text: C2 implants sleep 90%+ of the time - memory scanners look for implant signatures
Use `CreateTimerQueueTimer` to chain ROP: RW → encrypt → sleep → decrypt → RX
APC-based sleep obfuscation using `NtQueueApcThread`
Unmap implant memory entirely during sleep - nothing to scan
Encrypt all heap allocations, not just implant image
The encryption itself creates patterns - advanced EDRs detect timer-based chains

cards.title: API Unhooking
cards.summary: Remove EDR hooks from ntdll.dll - restore clean syscall stubs

items.text: Read clean ntdll.dll from disk, overwrite .text section of loaded ntdll - all hooks removed
Suspend all threads, unhook, resume - avoids race conditions
Read from `\KnownDlls\ntdll.dll` kernel object - always clean
Spawn suspended process → read its ntdll (before EDR hooks) → copy
EDRs check ntdll integrity - some re-hook after unhooking detected

cards.title: Call Stack Spoofing
cards.summary: Fake the call stack to hide where execution originated - defeat stack-walking detections

items.text: EDRs walk the call stack - return addresses pointing to unbacked memory = alert
Replace return addresses with pointers to legitimate module code
Desync the call stack before API calls, restore after
Before each sensitive API call, overwrite stack with legitimate RAs
Use TLS directory callbacks for execution - unusual call origin

cards.title: EDR-Specific Bypasses
cards.summary: Vendor-specific weaknesses for major EDR products

items.text: ~50+ excluded EXE names in registry - naming binary `apache.exe` prevents hook DLL loading
Manipulating system clock - actions don't appear in console (15min window)
Copy-paste of SAM/SYSTEM hives flagged, but drag-and-drop uses different API
Insert VEH handler with arg `0` (append) - S1 doesn't re-add its handler
Browse `\\.\PhysicalDrive0` in 7-Zip to copy SAM/SYSTEM - most EDRs don't monitor this
EDRSilencer: Uses Windows Filtering Platform to block EDR network communications
Deploy WDAC policy blocking EDR drivers → reboot → EDR fails to start

cards.title: Code Signing & Reputation Evasion
cards.summary: Abuse certificate trust and SmartScreen reputation to bypass static defenses

items.text: SmartScreen treats any certificate as less suspicious - expired certs work
Rules check for "unsigned" but expired certs return `errorExpired` - bypasses check
Find leaked OV certs on GitHub, VirusTotal, open S3 buckets (GrayhatWarfare)
Limelighter: Generate fake/spoofed code signatures for DLLs, EXEs, MSIs
Defender doesn't scan files >50MB. Falcon cloud ML default cutoff ~35MB

cards.title: Malware Virtualization & Anti-Analysis
cards.summary: Run malicious code in custom VM interpreters - evade static, behavioral, and memory analysis

items.text: riscy-business - run code in RISC-V virtual machine interpreter, no executable memory needed
Themida, VMProtect - production-grade code virtualization and packing
Load PE on top of legitimate module's memory space - code appears backed by legit DLL
Default Donut has detectable AMSI patching + 10KB signatured bootstrap. Remove aPLib, externalize loader
Prompt LLMs to reorder code, introduce junk with `volatile`/`register`

code.title: EDR Detection Layers & Bypasses
code.text:
LAYER 1: STATIC SIGNATURES
├── AV/YARA rules on disk          // Bypass: encryption, obfuscation, packing
└── Import table analysis         // Bypass: dynamic resolution, syscalls
LAYER 2: USERLAND HOOKS
├── ntdll.dll hooks               // Bypass: unhooking, direct syscalls
└── AMSI (amsi.dll)               // Bypass: patch AmsiScanBuffer, hardware BP
LAYER 3: ETW TELEMETRY
├── EtwEventWrite                 // Bypass: patch to ret, NtTraceEvent hook
└── Threat Intelligence ETW       // Bypass: disable provider GUID
LAYER 4: KERNEL CALLBACKS
├── PsSetCreateProcessNotifyRoutine  // Can't bypass from userland
└── ObRegisterCallbacks           // Process handle ops (LSASS access)
LAYER 5: MEMORY SCANNING
├── RWX region detection          // Bypass: RW → RX flip, no RWX
└── Unbacked memory execution     // Bypass: module stomping, phantom DLL
LAYER 6: BEHAVIORAL / CALL STACK
├── Call stack analysis           // Bypass: stack spoofing, return address overwrite
└── Suspicious API call chains    // Bypass: indirect execution, callbacks

title: // Process Injection Techniques
description: Running your code inside another process - the core tradecraft of any implant. Each technique has different detection signatures, OPSEC tradeoffs, and requirements.

cards.title: Classic Injection (VirtualAllocEx)
cards.summary: The textbook method - heavily detected but worth understanding as a baseline

items.text: Every step triggers kernel callbacks - cross-process handle + RWX + remote thread = instant alert
Process handle access (ObRegisterCallbacks), memory allocation, thread creation
In unmonitored environments or as learning exercise

cards.title: Module Stomping / Phantom DLL
cards.summary: Overwrite a legitimate DLL's .text section with shellcode - execution from backed memory

items.text: Load a benign DLL → overwrite its .text with shellcode → execute
Memory region shows as backed by a legitimate DLL on disk
Load a DLL that doesn't exist on disk (transaction rollback) - backed but no file
Choose a DLL that's normally loaded by the target process

cards.title: Threadless Injection
cards.summary: No thread creation or APC queue - hook APIs in target process to trigger shellcode naturally

items.text: Place hooks on regularly-called APIs in the target process
When the target process naturally calls the hooked API, shellcode triggers automatically
No CreateRemoteThread, no APC, no thread hijacking - purely event-driven
Not detected by any major vendor as of testing - fundamentally different from traditional injection
The gold standard for process injection

cards.title: Early Cascade Injection
cards.summary: Intercept process creation at the earliest stage - before EDR hooks are established

items.text: Intercept the DLL loading cascade during process initialization
Use debug flag instead of CREATE_SUSPENDED - different process creation path
Wins the race against EDR hook installation by operating earlier in the cascade
Use thread description API (`NtSetInformationThread`) to write shellcode via thread name primitive
Use INT3 + VEH to set DR0-DR3 debug registers - avoids ETW-Ti events

cards.title: APC Injection & Thread Pool
cards.summary: Queue shellcode as APC or via Windows Thread Pool for natural execution

items.text: Create process suspended → write shellcode → APC on main thread → resume
Early Bird executes before EDR DLL is loaded into the new process
Create work item pointing to shellcode - submitted to thread pool
Thread pool threads have legitimate call stacks - harder to distinguish from normal work
Used by Nighthawk C2 - very effective against call stack analysis

cards.title: Callback-based & PE File Injection
cards.summary: Use Windows API callbacks and Cordyceps technique for alternative execution

items.text: EnumFonts, EnumWindows, CreateFiber, CreateTimerQueueTimer, CertEnumSystemStore
No CreateThread/CreateRemoteThread - execution triggered by benign-looking API call
Reuse target PE's IAT and data sections, change execution flow - no process injection APIs
RedBackdoorer: Implements Cordyceps technique for PE file backdooring
Kernel-mode HTTP.sys API - no admin needed, shows as PID 4 (System)

title: // Lateral Movement
description: Moving through the network after initial compromise. Each method has different port requirements, authentication types, and OPSEC signatures.

callouts.title: Risk Levels:
callouts.body: PsExec (HIGH - service creation 7045), WMI execution (MEDIUM - WmiPrvSE parent), DCOM execution (LOW-MED), SCShell service config change (LOW - Event 7040, not 7045), Named pipe C2 (LOW - no new process). Prefer fileless and port-135-only techniques where possible.

cards.title: Pass-the-Hash / Pass-the-Ticket / Overpass
cards.summary: Reuse captured credentials without knowing plaintext passwords

items.text: Use NT hash directly via NTLM - works with SMB, WMI, WinRM, RDP (Restricted Admin)
Inject stolen Kerberos TGT/TGS - Rubeus `ptt /ticket:base64`
Use NT hash to request a Kerberos TGT - avoids environments blocking NTLM

MSFTRecon: Microsoft 365 reconnaissance - enumerate tenant information, domains, and services
ATEAM: NetSPI AWS enumeration - discover and map AWS resources from external perspective
Porch-Pirate: Postman workspace credential harvesting from public collections
API keys, OAuth tokens, database credentials, service account passwords

cards.title: Breach Intelligence & Email Harvesting
cards.summary: Leverage breach databases for credential discovery and password pattern analysis

items.text: Hudson Rock: Breach intelligence platform - compromised credentials and infostealer data
White Intel: Incident response intelligence - breach data correlated with target organizations
Analyze breached passwords from target org to build targeted wordlists
HunterScrape: Email harvesting from Hunter.io - extract corporate email addresses at scale
Prospeo: B2B email finder - discover professional email addresses for targeted phishing

cards.title: Distributed & Application Scanning
cards.summary: Cloud-based distributed reconnaissance at scale

items.text: Axiom: Cloud-based distributed recon - spin up fleet of scanning instances. Works with nmap, ffuf, nuclei
Moodle-Scanner: LuemmelSec's Moodle vulnerability scanner with self-updating via file hash cross-checks
udpz: SOCKS proxy-compatible UDP service scanner - scan UDP services through C2 SOCKS tunnels
DNS, SNMP, NTP, TFTP - often unmonitored and misconfigured on internal networks

cards.title: Stealthy AD Enumeration
cards.summary: Active Directory enumeration tools that minimize detection footprint

items.text: ShadowHound: PowerShell-based AD enumeration - no binary on disk, runs entirely in memory
SilentHound: Stealthy LDAP enumeration - minimal queries, low-noise AD data collection
BOFHound: BloodHound data collection via Beacon Object Files - inline execution, no fork & run
Adalanche: ACL visualization and analysis - identify attack paths through AD permission chains
These tools generate significantly less noise than SharpHound/bloodhound-python

title: // Password Cracking Infrastructure
description: Distributed cracking rigs, cloud GPU rental, wordlist generation, and rule development. Efficient password cracking is a force multiplier for every credential harvested during an engagement.

cards.title: Distributed Cracking Platforms
cards.summary: Scale password cracking across multiple nodes - serverless, on-prem, and GPU-accelerated

items.text: NPK: Serverless cracking platform - Terraform/Ansible deployment on AWS with auto-scaling GPU instances
Hashtopolis: On-prem distributed agent-based cracking - split work across multiple machines
hashcat: GPU-accelerated core cracking engine - supports 300+ hash types, rules, masks, and hybrid attacks

cards.title: Cloud GPU Rental
cards.summary: Rent GPU compute for cracking sessions - cost-effective alternative to building dedicated hardware

items.text: vast.ai: Cheapest GPU compute marketplace - rent consumer and datacenter GPUs on demand
RunPod: GPU instances optimized for ML workloads - easily repurposed for hashcat
SaladCloud: Distributed GPU network - leverage idle consumer GPUs for cracking
~$0.20-0.50/hr for consumer GPUs (RTX 3090/4090) vs $2-5/hr for datacenter A100s
Consumer GPUs offer best price/performance for most hash types; A100s for bcrypt/scrypt

cards.title: Wordlist Generation & Rules
cards.summary: Targeted wordlist creation and organization-specific rule development

items.text: Brutas: Handcrafted targeted wordlists - built from organization-specific intelligence
Skweez: Website scraper wordlist generator - extract terms from target's web presence
WikiRaider: Wikipedia-based wordlist generation
Season+Year (`Winter2025!`), Company+Numbers (`Contoso123`), Keyboard walks
Crack initial batch → analyze patterns → refine rules → crack more
Google Cloud BigQuery for massive rainbow table lookups - instant cracking
